statement: A solid is a group or component with a finite closed volume (no missing faces, every edge shared by exactly two faces); Entity Info reports Solid status, volume and offers Solid Inspector style diagnosis.

source.ref: Solid definition and solid status check

superiority: Diagnoses and auto-repairs non-manifold, flipped and open meshes with a report.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/inspecting-entity Acceptance sketch: Open and closed fixtures: solid flag true only for manifold watertight groups; volume equals closed form within 1e-9 relative. RW5-SUDRAW 2026-11-25: acceptance[0] is kernel test extra::SuSolidFlagIsTrueOnlyForTheWatertightBodyWithTheClosedFormVolume (dino8-kernel/tests/extra/sudraw_solid_tools_tests.cpp); oracle is closed forms and counts: a 3 x 4 x 5 box has volume 60 and 12 edges each in exactly two faces; the same box without its top has exactly 4 naked edges; the Register row statement is quoted at the head of the test; covers: closed fixture reports solid with volume 60 to 1e-9 relative, the 5-face open fixture is not a solid (4 naked edges) and refuses the closed-volume query, putting the top back makes it solid again; untested: the Entity Info panel text and the repair offers of the row. Not credit: status open, evidence null until CI.

statement: Outer Shell merges overlapping solids keeping only the external faces and returns a group, reducing geometry.
superiority: Exact boolean on curved and NURBS solids.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Two overlapping boxes: result volume equals analytic union volume and has no internal faces. RW5-SUDRAW 2026-11-25: acceptance[0] is kernel test extra::SuOuterShellOfTwoBoxesKeepsOnlyTheExternalFacesOfTheUnion (dino8-kernel/tests/extra/sudraw_solid_tools_tests.cpp); oracle is inclusion-exclusion by interval overlap (64 + 64 - 18 = 110) and the skin of each box outside the other (96 + 96 - 21 - 21 = 150) re-derived in the test by interval arithmetic; the Register row statement is quoted at the head of the test; covers: union of two overlapping boxes: volume 110, surface 150 (no internal face), 12 faces after coplanar pieces are merged (fewer than the raw result), every edge in two faces; untested: the group wrapper of the result and curved operands. Not credit: status open, evidence null until CI.

statement: Union merges two or more solids into a single solid group, keeping the outer geometry and interior.
superiority: Union is order independent and non-destructive when desired.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Union of three overlapping spheres: volume by inclusion-exclusion within 1e-6 relative. RW5-SUDRAW 2026-11-25: acceptance[0] is kernel test extra::SuUnionOfThreeOverlappingSolidsFollowsInclusionExclusion (dino8-kernel/tests/extra/sudraw_solid_tools_tests.cpp); oracle is inclusion-exclusion V = sum Vi - sum Vij + Vabc with every term from interval overlaps (64 + 64 + 80 - 18 - 18 - 18 + 8 = 162); the Register row statement is quoted at the head of the test; covers: union of three overlapping boxes: one valid closed solid of volume 162 to 1e-9; untested: three overlapping SPHERES to 1e-6 relative (the curved-solid engine measured about 1 percent on sphere pairs, so the sphere case is not covered). Not credit: status open, evidence null until CI. QC 2026-11-25 (independent review, confirmed by two skeptics: overclaim): credit withheld because the linked test covers less than the row statement or sketch. Finding: SOLID-0003 is credited by a union of three boxes. The sketch is 'Union of three overlapping spheres: volume by inclusion-exclusion within 1e-6 relative'. The extra acceptance entry T-SKETCHUP-SOLID-0003-FULLSCOPE is a deliberate placeholder for the full-scope test.

statement: Procedural Union combines solids into a procedural component, nesting each union so every part stays editable.
superiority: Procedural history is a first-class editable tree.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/release-notes/sketchup-desktop-20270 Acceptance sketch: Edit one operand after union; result updates and volume matches new closed form.

statement: Subtract removes the second selected solid by the first (cutter) and deletes the cutter; selection order matters.
superiority: Keeps cutter optional in model as a hidden operand.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Cylinder from box: volume equals box minus cylinder within 1e-6 relative; order reversal swaps the roles. RW5-SUDRAW 2026-11-25: acceptance[0] is kernel test extra::SuSubtractOrderSwapsTheRolesAndTheCylinderCutMatchesPiRSquaredH (dino8-kernel/tests/extra/sudraw_solid_tools_tests.cpp); oracle is closed forms: A - T = 64 - 8 = 56 and T - A = 16 - 8 = 8 from interval overlaps; cylinder minus box = pi r^2 (6 - 4) = 2 pi; the Register row statement is quoted at the head of the test; covers: subtract in both operand orders on boxes (56 versus 8, closed solids) and a cylinder cut by a box (2 pi within 1e-6 relative on the sealed exact volume); untested: box minus cylinder (the exact curved engine does not seal that direction; the application falls back to the mesh engine) and deletion of the cutter. Not credit: status open, evidence null until CI. QC 2026-11-25 (independent review, confirmed by two skeptics: overclaim): credit withheld because the linked test covers less than the row statement or sketch. Finding: SOLID-0005's sketch is 'Cylinder from box: volume equals box minus cylinder within 1e-6 relative; order reversal swaps the roles'. The curved half of the test computes the opposite operand order. The extra acceptance entry T-SKETCHUP-SOLID-0005-FULLSCOPE is a deliberate placeholder for the full-scope test.

statement: Procedural Subtract creates a procedural component preserving the target attributes while cutting.
superiority: Operand parameters exposed as drivers.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/release-notes/sketchup-desktop-20270 Acceptance sketch: Move the cutter after subtraction; cut position updates.

statement: Trim cuts the second solid with the first and keeps the first in the model.
superiority: Same with undo and cutter retention flags.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Trim a box by a plane-bounded solid; remaining volume equals closed form, cutter unchanged.

statement: Intersect leaves only the volume shared by two solids.
superiority: Exact for surfaces of revolution.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Two cylinders: intersection volume equals closed form (Steinmetz) within tolerance. RW5-SUDRAW 2026-11-25: acceptance[0] is kernel test extra::SuIntersectLeavesTheSharedVolumeOfTwoSolids (dino8-kernel/tests/extra/sudraw_solid_tools_tests.cpp); oracle is closed forms: boxes share [2,4] x [1,4] x [1,4] (volume 18, surface 42, corners (2,1,1) and (4,4,4)); two perpendicular unit cylinders share 16 r^3 / 3; the Register row statement is quoted at the head of the test; covers: intersect of two boxes exact to 1e-9 (6-face solid, volume, surface, corners) and of two crossing cylinders to 1 percent (measured 0.54 percent; the curved-solid engine is not tighter than that); untested: a tighter Steinmetz tolerance. Not credit: status open, evidence null until CI.

statement: Procedural Intersect keeps the shared volume as a procedural component.
superiority: Operand history is a first-class editable tree, so any intermediate can be inspected or replaced.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Intersect two overlapping solids procedurally; move one operand and verify the result updates to the new analytic volume.

statement: Split divides overlapping solids along the intersection into separate pieces.
superiority: Piece naming and classification inheritance.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Two boxes: three pieces whose volumes sum to union volume. RW5-SUDRAW 2026-11-25: acceptance[0] is kernel test extra::SuSplitOfTwoOverlappingBoxesGivesThreePiecesSummingToTheUnion (dino8-kernel/tests/extra/sudraw_solid_tools_tests.cpp); oracle is inclusion-exclusion by interval overlap (46 + 18 + 46 = 110) and the surfaces of the pieces (union surface 150 plus every interface face twice, 234); the Register row statement is quoted at the head of the test; covers: the three pieces A - B, A n B and B - A of two overlapping boxes: closed solids, volumes 46, 18, 46 summing to the union, surfaces consistent with the interfaces; untested: the Split command as one step in the application (the pieces here come from three planar booleans). Not credit: status open, evidence null until CI.

statement: Solid tools are available in Tools menu, Solid Tools toolbar, Procedures toolbar and context menu with preselection.

source.ref: Solid tools via context menu and Tools menu and toolbars

superiority: Single command search entry.
notes: Acceptance sketch: All entry points produce equal results for the same selection order.

statement: Procedural solid tools preserve attributes of the target; booleans carry materials of originating faces.

source.ref: Solid tools attribute and material preservation

superiority: Attributes merge rules configurable.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/modeling-complex-3d-shapes-solid-tools Acceptance sketch: Boolean of two materials: result faces keep source materials.

statement: Solid operations apply to groups and components with transforms; nested solids are handled and results are groups.

source.ref: Solid tools on components with nested geometry

superiority: Handles non-uniform scale correctly.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Boolean of a nested component under a scaled parent: transformed volume correct.

statement: Web client provides a Solid Inspector that highlights and fixes problems making a model non-solid.
superiority: Desktop-native, fast on million-face models.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Fixture with 5 defect classes; each is listed and the repaired model is a solid.

statement: Copy Along places copies of a group or component along a whole path as a procedural component, with distribution by count, distance or gap.
superiority: Distribution along any curve with arc-length parameterization.
notes: Acceptance sketch: 10 copies by count along a 10 m path: spacing is path length over (n-1) within 1e-9. RW5-SUDRAW 2026-11-25: acceptance[0] is kernel test extra::SuCopyAlongTenCopiesByCountAreSpacedPathLengthOverNMinusOne (dino8-kernel/tests/extra/sudraw_curve_tools_tests.cpp); oracle is closed forms: copy k at start + k (end - start) / (n - 1), consecutive spacing 10 / 9 along a path of length 10; the Register row statement is quoted at the head of the test; covers: ten copies by count along a straight 10 m path (no rotation), vertex positions and spacing within 1e-9; untested: distribution by distance or gap, a procedural component that stays editable, and the bent path case of the other Copy Along rows. Not credit: status open, evidence null until CI.

statement: Copy Along each segment distributes copies per path segment with absolute or relative margin modes.
superiority: Per-segment parameter overrides.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Segments 3 m and 5 m, 2 copies each; margin applied per segment exactly.

statement: Copy Along on corners places copies at the path's corner vertices with orientation.
superiority: Corner orientation options (bisector, normal, tangent).
notes: Acceptance sketch: Rectangular path: 4 copies at corners, orientation matches corner bisector.

statement: Orientation modes yaw-only or yaw and pitch along sloping paths.

source.ref: Copy Along orientation (stairlike yaw only and roadlike yaw and pitch)

superiority: Full Frenet or user-defined up-vector frames.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Sloped path: stairlike keeps vertical axis; roadlike matches slope within 1e-9.

statement: Procedural components expose parameters in Entity Info and can be edited, nested and reused like components.

source.ref: Procedural component editing in Entity Info

superiority: Parameters are bindable to the model data graph.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Change parameters; geometry regenerates deterministically (same input, same output hash).

statement: Procedures menu and toolbar offer Copy Along, Follow Me and solid operations.
superiority: Fully customizable ribbon and command palette with search across all procedures.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Enable the Procedural Tools toolbar through View > Toolbars; restart; the toolbar state persists.
